Lawrence C. Kingsland (April 11, 1884 – February 1, 1970) was an American patent lawyer and government official who served as the United States Commissioner of Patents from 1947 to 1949.
Early life and career
Kingsland was born in St. Louis and attended Washington University in St. Louis, receiving a law degree from the Washington University School of Law in 1908. Before entering federal service, he practiced patent law in St. Louis for nearly four decades.
Commissioner of Patents
President Harry S. Truman appointed Kingsland commissioner of patents, and he took the oath of office on September 10, 1947. He had previously advised the government of the Philippines in drafting patent and trademark laws. In 1947, the Patent Office Advisory Committee was reactivated during his tenure.
